content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Understand upper and lower bounds for rounded values
Calculate upper and lower bounds for calculations
When a measurement is rounded, the original value could have been any value within a range.
tell us the limits of this range. This is a
topic essential for understanding measurement accuracy and error analysis.
Explore bounds and error intervals — calculate upper and lower bounds for rounded measurements using the interactive visualisation below.
When a value is rounded to a given degree of accuracy:
is the smallest value that rounds to that number
is the smallest value that would round UP to the next number
For a value rounded to a given unit:
We use $<$ for the upper bound because exactly 7.5 would round UP to 8.
Degree of accuracy = 100 m (since 2 s.f. means nearest 100)
A length is 5.8 m to 1 d.p. Find the bounds.
A weight is 200 g to the nearest 10 g. Find the bounds.
uses inequality notation to show the range of possible values.
The notation uses $\leq$ for lower bound and $<$ for upper bound.
When combining measurements, use bounds appropriately:
To get a big answer, divide big by small. To get a small answer, divide small by big.
A rectangle has length 8.5 cm and width 4.3 cm, both measured to 1 d.p. Calculate the bounds for the area.
A car travels 156 miles (to 3 s.f.) in 2.4 hours (to 2 s.f.). Calculate the bounds for the average speed.
The length of a rope is 12 m to the nearest metre. A piece of length 3 m (to the nearest metre) is cut off. Find the bounds for the remaining length.
The density of a material is calculated using $\rho = \frac{m}{V}$. The mass is 45.6 g (3 s.f.) and volume is 8.2 cm³ (2 s.f.). Calculate the bounds for density.
A square has area 64 cm² (to 2 s.f.). Find the bounds for the side length.
When stating a final answer, consider how many figures are justified by the bounds.
If bounds for an area are 35.9125 cm² and 37.1925 cm², we cannot claim precision beyond these bounds.
The area lies between approximately 36 and 37 cm².
Stating the answer as 36 cm² or 37 cm² (to 2 s.f.) would be appropriate.
Upper bound = given value + degree of accuracy
A length is given as 5.3 cm by truncation to 1 d.p.
A length is 6.7 cm to 1 d.p. State the lower and upper bounds.
Write the error interval for 450 rounded to the nearest 10.
For $a = 5$ (nearest integer) and $b = 3$ (nearest integer), find bounds for $a \times b$.
give the range of possible values for rounded measurements
Bounds are found by adding/subtracting half the degree of accuracy
max = UB + UB, min = LB + LB
max = UB - LB, min = LB - UB
max = UB × UB, min = LB × LB
max = UB ÷ LB, min = LB ÷ UB
